reading.body:
James v. Meow Media is the 2002 Sixth Circuit precedent that AI harm suits are now being answered with, almost paragraph for paragraph.

The holding has three parts. Makers of video games and films owed no duty of care for a school shooting allegedly influenced by their content. The crime was not sufficiently foreseeable. Intangible media content is not a product for strict liability. The court leaned on the shooter's independent criminal act as a superseding cause.

That structure maps onto the current docket. Six live cases, Grant and Askins against OpenAI entities and four against Character Technologies, test whether a system that interacts, personalises and responds in the moment can still be cast as inert media. The defense playbook is the same: no duty to unforeseeable victims of a user's acts, superseding criminal conduct, content is not a product.

What the data does not show is any ruling in those live cases. It gives the precedent, the live matter count, and the seam being tested, not the outcomes. The distinction the newer suits press is architectural rather than editorial, and nothing here records how any court has resolved it.

section.name: AI Case Law: The Precedents Behind the Defenses
